aspect: No right to work is the whole of it
description: Without work authorisation there is no lawful income, which means informal work at whatever rate is offered, with no recourse for non-payment because complaining requires identifying yourself.
energy_note: Working, and unable to say so, or to be paid properly.

description: Chronic conditions go unmanaged because registration requires status. The diabetes, the fibroids, the hypertension all progress until they qualify as an emergency, which is the most expensive possible point of treatment.
energy_note: Waiting until it is an emergency, because that is the only door.

description: Signing at a police station or reporting centre at intervals, with the possibility of detention at each one, means no job with fixed hours and no journey longer than the gap between reports.
time_note: Days per year consumed by reporting.
energy_note: A life sized to fit between two signings.

description: She arrived at twenty-six. She is thirty-seven. She has been refused twice, appealed once, made fresh submissions twice, and been detained for nine days in 2021. She has an English accent now. She has never had a National Insurance number.
energy_note: A decade spent being about to be deported.

description: Every second Tuesday, 9am, forty minutes on two buses. She has done it sixty-one times. She has never been detained at one and she has never once walked in without considering that she might be.
energy_note: Sixty-one Tuesdays of walking in wondering.
